subject: Cigarette prices to drop $30 under Coalition plan
posts:
A radical plan to slash cigarette taxes by 80% is pitched as a war on crime, but critics warn it's a deadly gamble.

Cigarette prices to drop $30 under Coalition plan
Evidence: Slashed crime, Increased smoking deaths, Political survival
#Aletheia #AusPol 🌐

The Coalition claims that cutting the tobacco excise by 80% will destroy the multi-billion-dollar black market, stop violent firebombings, and lower prices for struggling household budgets.
Stated Judgement: (+1.00, +0.80) — Greater Good

In reality, slashing cigarette prices to $6 a pack reverses decades of public health progress, risking a massive surge in smoking rates and preventable deaths, all to claw back votes from One Nation.
Resulting Judgement: (-0.85, -0.75) — Greater Evil

Verdict: FAIL — Fall into Destruction. The Coalition trades public health and human lives for a desperate bid to counter One Nation's rising popularity.

Integrity: Trustworthy (Hypocrisy: 1.25, Uncertainty z: 1)

Sub-Audits Breakdown:
- Angus Taylor: FAIL (-0.85, -0.75) — Pretextual law-and-order framing.
- Public Health Impact: FAIL (-0.90, -0.80) — Reverses decades of anti-smoking progress.
The Coalition has proposed an 80% cut to tobacco excise, reducing a standard pack to $6, claiming it will undercut the illicit market currently fueling a wave of violent retail firebombings.

The Poison:
While undercutting the black market could temporarily reduce gang-related firebombings, making cigarettes dirt-cheap will inevitably hook a new generation of smokers and cost thousands of lives.

The Breakdown & Plane Error:
This is a classic WHAT vs WHO error. The Coalition frames the issue purely as a law-enforcement problem (WHAT), while ignoring the catastrophic physical toll on the citizens (WHO) who will suffer from increased tobacco addiction.

Social Physics Analysis:
By using the genuine threat of organized crime as a pretext, the Coalition attempts to justify a policy that actively harms public health. This projection shifts the blame entirely onto government failure while hiding their own political desperation.

The Trajectory: The Path of Fall into Destruction.
When you map the gap between stated intentions and ground-level results, it plots a direct trajectory toward Greater Evil. The policy sacrifices long-term societal health for short-term political survival.

The Unavoidable Truth: Dirt-cheap cigarettes will increase smoking rates and deaths.

The Unavoidable Lie: This policy is purely about stopping crime rather than winning back conservative voters.
